claim_text: Indonesia GP-to-population ratio is approximately 0.6 per 1,000.

new_sources.key_data: WHO SEARO HRH Country Profile (Sep 2024): combined doctors+nurses+midwives density = 15.6 per 10,000. Medical doctors sub-component visible at approximately 6–7 per 10,000 (0.6–0.7 per 1,000) for ALL physicians, not GP-only.
Citing WHO 2019 data via IndexMundi: Indonesia all-doctor ratio = 0.47 per 1,000. No GP/specialist breakdown. Timor Leste 0.77, Philippines 0.60 for context.
World Bank Physicians per 1,000 people — Indonesia. Page confirmed to have data through 2023; exact value ~0.7 per 1,000 for ALL physicians per search snippet.
WHO GHO indicator: Density of physicians per 10,000. Indonesia most recent year on record: 2020. Consistent with ~7.4 per 10,000 = 0.74 per 1,000 for all physicians.

critical_distinction.all_physicians_per_1000: ~0.47 (WHO 2019) to ~0.74 (WHO 2020) — range due to year and methodology differences
critical_distinction.gp_only_estimated_per_1000: ~0.4 — derived: GPs (dokter umum) are ~61% of all doctors per Indonesian MoH data; if all-doctor = 0.64, GP share ≈ 0.39
critical_distinction.claim_figure_0.6: Appears to reflect the all-physician figure for a mid-range year, NOT the GP-only figure
critical_distinction.implication: The 0.6/1,000 figure is plausible for ALL physicians in a mid-period (2020–2022), but the GP-only (dokter umum) ratio is materially lower at ~0.4/1,000

suggested_revision: Replace claim with: 'Indonesia's physician density is approximately 0.47–0.74 per 1,000 population (all doctors, WHO 2019–2022); the GP-only (dokter umum) ratio is lower still, estimated at ~0.4 per 1,000, since GPs constitute roughly 61% of the total physician pool. The commonly cited 0.6 figure refers to all physicians, not GPs specifically.'
reasoning: WHO multilateral and World Bank sources confirm the all-physician density is 0.47–0.74 per 1,000 (year-dependent); the 0.6 claim is plausible for all physicians but incorrectly attributed to GPs specifically. Indonesian MoH data shows GPs are ~61% of all doctors, placing the GP-only ratio closer to 0.4/1,000 — a material distinction for the PP1/PP2 arguments about primary care access.
